description:
A team of one with a crew of furballs, building the Space Mission Design Game as a web game anyone can play. Plan a mission from launch to the Moon or Mars with plush explorers led by two Polish elephants, two captains, and a lunar rover, balancing mass, power, budget, data, and communications.

We warmly welcome Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Medium) as a valued member of the team.

The Seattle home and furball family join in, on a visit to North Carolina.
summary: Furball Frenzy: Mission Control is a space mission design game for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players pick a launcher, instruments, a solar array, and an antenna for two Polish elephants' rover bound for the lunar south pole. Six gauges, mass, power, budget, data, communications, and time, update on every choice, and the launch is locked with a plain explanation until the design can fly. A launched mission is told as a story by the furball crew, with a go or no-go at the final checks, trouble in space that is fixed or ends in a safe return, a splashdown, and a debrief that explains why it worked or failed, what was left on the table, and which real NASA surface mission the rover most resembles, with linked NASA sources. There is no single perfect design, and anyone can replay with one change. It matters because mission design is a game of trade-offs, and this makes those trade-offs something a student, a family, or a judge can feel in 30 seconds, on a phone, with no account.
details:
What it does: a playable mission design game, build, launch, watch the story, read the debrief, change one thing, try again. A "Judges, start here" button has the elephants design and launch a mission in about 30 seconds.

How it works: a tested pure TypeScript simulation checks that the rover fits the launcher, the array covers the lunar day, and the antenna carries the science home. The story is a script generated from the simulation result, so every outcome has its own scenes. The debrief compares the design to six real NASA surface missions by mass and instruments.

Benefits: teaches trade-offs and learning from failure, runs on a phone, needs no account, and is playful for younger players while the debrief is sourced for older ones.

Tools and languages: TypeScript, React, Next.js, and Tailwind on the front, Python and FastAPI for the crew API, Vitest and Playwright for tests, Storybook for components, Docker, Cloudflare Tunnel on an Oracle VM, Flodesk for the email sign-up, built with Claude Sonnet 5.5 as the daily coding collaborator with a little Fable 5.2 magic sprinkled in.
